samples.summary: New doc claims dot-segment ids are always refused and that ids are always one segment, but the `--dry-run` path bypasses `seg()` entirely
samples.evidence: The delta adds to docs/design/cli.md an unconditional error-matrix row — "Workspace / document / tab / cell id is `.` or `..` | 1 | ERROR | ... (refused before any request is sent)" — and prose that "Every id the client interpolates into a request URL ... is percent-encoded". The dry-run preview, which §8.2 defines as "prints the request that would be sent", builds its URL independently in `printDryRun` (`${server}/api/v1/workspaces/${config.workspace}${path}`) from raw, unencoded ids supplied by the command layer (e.g. packages/cli/src/commands/cells.ts:55, docs.ts:188, notes.ts:140). So `wafflebase docs content '..' --dry-run` exits 0 and prints a traversing URL rather than the documented ERROR/exit 1, and the previewed URL does not match the URL the real call would send for any id needing encoding. Either the doc row needs a dry-run carve-out or `printDryRun` should share the same segment encoding.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. `printDryRun` (packages/cli/src/client/dry-run.ts:12-13) assembles `${server}/api/v1/workspaces/${config.workspace}${path}` with no percent-encoding and no dot-segment refusal; `seg()` exists only in packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts:71-76 and is applied only on HttpClient paths (:108, :239, :392). Command handlers interpolate raw argv ids into the dry-run path and return before any client call (commands/docs.ts:184-191, commands/cells.ts:51-58, commands/tabs.ts:47-50 and :71-75), so `docs content '..' --dry-run` exits 0 and prints a traversing URL. No guard exists: commands/root.ts:24-40 validates nothing, and the only documented pre-dry-run validation in the repo is the unrelated tab-`type` check at commands/tabs.ts:34-43. Meanwhile docs/design/cli.md:1073 states the `.`/`..` ERROR row unconditionally, :1087-1104 claims every interpolated id is encoded and dot segments are refused outright, :246-248 extends it to the workspace id, and §8.2 (:813-816) defines --dry-run as printing "the request that would be sent". The documented behavior and the shipped dry-run path genuinely disagree — a spec/design-doc conformance gap of `major` kind in this lens; no not-present, already-guarded, or out-of-scope ground applies.

searchedFor: grep 'Invalid path segment' across docs/ and packages/cli
finding.summary: The new hard-failure mode introduced by `seg()` is not recorded in the design doc. `HttpClient` now throws `Invalid path segment: ".."` (a plain `Error`, so it surfaces as code `ERROR`) for a document/tab/cell/workspace id of `.` or `..`, and silently percent-encodes every other id. §10's Error Matrix — which this same PR rewrites in detail, down to 80/500/4000-character bounds — has no row for it, and §3/§8 say nothing about id encoding. The PR documents its error contract meticulously while leaving the one new agent-visible failure it introduces undocumented.

verdict.reason: The finding claims §10's Error Matrix has no row for the new seg() hard-failure and that the doc says nothing about id encoding. Both are false. docs/design/cli.md:1073 is a row in §10's Error Matrix reading "| Workspace / document / tab / cell id is `.` or `..` | 1 | ERROR | \"Invalid path segment: \\\"..\\\"\" (refused before any request is sent) |", matching packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts:71-76 field-for-field (exit 1, plain Error so code ERROR, exact message text, thrown before any request). Beyond the matrix row, docs/design/cli.md:1087-1096 documents the id-encoding contract in prose under the heading "Ids are one path segment each.", naming seg() and its source file and giving the ../../../../workspaces/w/api-keys/k example; docs/design/cli.md:1098-1104 documents exactly the point alleged missing — that encodeURIComponent cannot pin `.`/`..`, that they are refused outright, that this "is the matrix's ERROR row above: a plain throw before the request is built (nothing reaches the network), and therefore the classifier's default code rather than a code of its own", and that every other id is encoded and sent. This documentation is in the same passage as the 80/500/4000-character bounds table (cli.md:1114-1119) the finding cites as the contrast case. The reviewer reports grepping 'Invalid path segment' across docs/ and finding nothing, but that grep's first documentation hit is docs/design/cli.md:1073. No design-fit or design-doc-discipline violation: the behavior is recorded in the canonical subsystem doc, not a parallel file.
